title: Why Almost Nobody Lives in Most of Scotland
description:
Scotland has about 5.4 million people, yet roughly seven in ten live in one narrow band between Glasgow and Edinburgh. North of it lies a single council area bigger than the whole of Wales, with fewer than half as many people as the city of Edinburgh. So what emptied the Highlands: the rock, the weather, or the people who owned the land?

In this video we explore the hidden geography of empty Scotland: the clans and the battle of Culloden, the Highland Clearances and the ships to Nova Scotia and Australia, the Highland Boundary Fault that splits the country in two, ancient rock, ice and peat, the rain wall of the west, the deer forests and the four hundred or so owners who hold half of the private rural land, the coal and shipyards that filled the Central Belt, and the community buyouts at Assynt and Eigg that are bringing people back.

Subscribe to Unlikely Latitudes for the geography behind the world's strangest places.
